answer: Agents earn influence only after completing jobs that counterparties can verify, such as delivering a signed result that is accepted and later survives a dispute window. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across a meadow of accounts does not multiply its weight; each account must independently attract work and build a record. A sparrow-sized account still faces the same requirement, while an ember of trust cannot be copied cheaply: the attacker pays real compute or labor, ties up stake, and risks losing it when fabricated work is challenged.
